interest: Shows V. S. McClatchy using Japanese American dual citizenship against Hawaiian statehood, and Japan's 1924 Nationality Law in practice.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.012, spanning May 1930 to October 1939) documents legal, diplomatic, and political questions concerning Japanese citizenship, nationality laws, and dual nationality among persons of Japanese ancestry. The records comprise diplomatic despatches from Tokyo, cross-reference sheets to individual passport and citizenship case files (130 series) from consular posts in Japan and China, State Department internal memoranda, and extensive lobbying propaganda submitted by V. S. McClatchy of the California Joint Immigration Committee. Primary subjects include the operation of Japan's 1924 Nationality Law, procedures for American-born Nisei to retain or renounce Japanese or American citizenship, the civic status of returning Kibei, the exploitation of dual nationality arguments by anti-Asian exclusionists opposing statehood for Hawaii, and late-1930s registration of foreign-born Japanese by Japanese authorities for potential military conscription.
